preconditions.expression: all(line.strip() == '' or (line.strip().isdigit() and 1 <= int(line.strip()) <= 500000) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() != '')
preconditions.description: The first line is a positive integer (number of test cases) between 1 and 500,000. Empty lines separate test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(len(test_case) == 2 for test_case in [input.splitlines()[i:i+2] for i in range(1, len(input.splitlines()), 3) if i+1 < len(input.splitlines())])
preconditions.description: Each test case consists of exactly two non-empty lines: the first is an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 500,000), and the second is a string of length n composed of 'V', 'K', and '?' characters.

preconditions.expression: all(len(s) == int(n) for n, s in [input.splitlines()[i:i+2] for i in range(1, len(input.splitlines()), 3) if i+1 < len(input.splitlines())])
preconditions.description: The length of the string in each test case matches the integer n provided in the first line of the test case.

preconditions.expression: all(all(c in {'V', 'K', '?'} for c in s) for n, s in [input.splitlines()[i:i+2] for i in range(1, len(input.splitlines()), 3) if i+1 < len(input.splitlines())])
preconditions.description: Each character in the string is either 'V', 'K', or '?'.

postconditions.description: For each test case, the output consists of exactly two lines: the first line is the count of possible periods, and the second line is the sorted list of possible periods.

postconditions.expression: all(output_lines[2 * i] == str(len(set(possible_periods))) and output_lines[2 * i + 1] == ' '.join(map(str, sorted(possible_periods))) for i, possible_periods in enumerate(compute_possible_periods(test_cases)))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the first output line is the count of distinct possible periods, and the second line is the sorted list of these periods. A period d is valid if there exists at least one way to replace all '?' with 'V' or 'K' such that the resulting string has period d.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= d <= n for d in possible_periods for n, s in test_cases)
postconditions.description: Every possible period d must satisfy 1 ≤ d ≤ n, where n is the length of the string in the test case.

postconditions.expression: all(all(s[i] == s[(i + d) % n] for i in range(n)) for d in possible_periods for n, s in test_cases for s in generate_all_possible_strings(n, s))
postconditions.description: A period d is valid for a test case if there exists at least one string s' (obtained by replacing '?' with 'V' or 'K') such that s'[i] == s'[(i + d) % n] for all i in 0..n-1.
